findings.title: One failing SendGrid cancel aborts the whole cancellation loop and prevents all row deletions
findings.body: The cancellation loop (`for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)`) is wrapped in a single try/catch. The `await client.request(...)` call is the first statement in the loop body, so any failure for one reminder (invalid/expired `batch_id`, a batch that is already in `cancel` status, a 401, or SendGrid's 100-pending-cancellation cap being reached) throws out of the loop. Consequences: (a) every remaining reminder in `remindersToCancel` is skipped for this run, (b) `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` on line 74 is never reached, so even the reminders that *were* successfully cancelled keep `cancelled = true` in the DB, and (c) on the next run the same poison record is fetched again and fails again, so cancellation is permanently broken for every reminder behind it. Since the batch row is never deleted after a successful cancel in this scenario, re-cancelling an already-cancelled batch on the next run is itself likely to error, making the deadlock self-sustaining. Each iteration needs its own try/catch (and the delete should happen per-item), so one bad record cannot block the rest.

findings.title: remindersToCancel query is not restricted to EMAIL reminders or to rows with a referenceId
findings.body: `prisma.workflowReminder.findMany({ where: { cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { lte: ... } } })` has no `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL` filter and no `referenceId: { not: null }` filter, unlike the `deleteMany` above it. Any non-email row (or any row with a null `referenceId`) that ever ends up with `cancelled = true` will be POSTed to `/v3/user/scheduled_sends` with a Twilio SID or `null` as `batch_id`. SendGrid will reject it, and because of the single try/catch around the loop that aborts all remaining cancellations (see the loop issue), one such row permanently breaks email cancellation. There is also no `take` limit, so a large backlog is processed sequentially with one HTTP request each, risking a serverless timeout mid-loop.

findings.title: Deferring cancellation to a 15-minute cron leaves reminders that are due soon uncancellable
findings.body: Cancellation is now only performed by this cron for reminders whose `scheduledDate` is within the next hour, and the `deleteMany` at line 34 unconditionally removes every EMAIL reminder with `scheduledDate <= now` (including rows with `cancelled = true`) before the cancellation block runs. If a booking is cancelled or rescheduled less than one cron interval before the reminder's send time (e.g. 10 minutes before), the next run happens after `scheduledDate` has passed: the row is deleted by `deleteMany` and the reminder email is delivered. Even when the run lands a few minutes before the send time, SendGrid only honours cancellation of a scheduled send up to ~10 minutes before `send_at`, so the cancel request is rejected. This is a regression versus cancelling immediately and reintroduces exactly the symptom this PR is meant to fix for short-notice cancellations.

findings.title: client.setApiKey() is never called in this handler, so the new cancel requests may be unauthenticated
findings.body: This file only calls `sgMail.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)`. `@sendgrid/mail` keeps its own internal client instance, whereas the `client` default export from `@sendgrid/client` used on line 57 (and line 188) is a separate singleton; `emailReminderManager.ts` explicitly calls `client.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` for this reason. Unless the key is set on that singleton by some other imported module, every `client.request()` here runs without an Authorization header and returns 401 — which, combined with the loop-wide try/catch, means no scheduled email is ever cancelled and the entire fix silently does nothing (only a `console.log`). Add `client.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` next to `sgMail.setApiKey`.

findings.title: immediateDelete path has no fallback and leaves the WorkflowReminder row behind
findings.body: In the `immediateDelete` branch the SendGrid cancel request is issued and the function returns without deleting the reminder row and without setting `cancelled = true`. Two problems: (1) if the request fails — which is precisely what happens when SendGrid's limit of 100 pending cancellations is hit, the scenario this PR describes — the error is swallowed by the outer `catch` and nothing records the intent to cancel, so the new cron fallback will never pick the reminder up and the reminder email is still delivered; (2) on success the row stays in the DB with `scheduled = true` and a dead `referenceId` until the cron's `deleteMany` eventually removes it, whereas the previous code deleted it. At minimum this branch should also mark/delete the row so there is a retry path.

findings.title: Reschedules still use the immediate SendGrid cancel, so rescheduled-booking reminders remain broken
findings.body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` passes `immediateDelete = true` for the reschedule path. The PR's own diagnosis is that immediate `POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends { status: "cancel" }` calls accumulate as pending cancellations and start failing once 100 are pending. Rescheduling is one of the two cases named in the PR title, and it is a high-volume path, so it keeps filling that quota and keeps failing silently (the error is only `console.log`ged in `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`), which both leaves the old reminder scheduled and can push the quota over the limit so that other cancellations (including the cron's) fail too. Reschedules should use the same deferred `cancelled = true` mechanism as cancellations.

findings.title: Reminder cancellation promises are not awaited, so the cancelled flag may never be persisted
findings.body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...)`/`deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)` are async but are invoked inside a `forEach` without awaiting, and the promises are no longer collected into `prismaPromises` as the deleted `remindersToDelete` array was. The whole fix now depends on a DB write (`cancelled = true`) performed in a floating promise; in a serverless deployment the function can be frozen/terminated once the handler returns, so the update can be lost and the reminder email will still be sent. The same pattern exists in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx` (requestReschedule) and `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx`. In `handleNewBooking.ts` the surrounding `try/catch` (lines 964-975) is additionally dead code: because the calls are not awaited, it can never catch their failures. These calls should be awaited (e.g. `await Promise.all(reminders.map(...))`).

findings.title: cancelled column is nullable with no default and no index for the cron query
findings.body: `cancelled Boolean?` (and the matching migration `ADD COLUMN "cancelled" BOOLEAN` with no default) gives the column three states (null/false/true) where only a boolean flag is needed, so consumers must remember that `cancelled: false` and `cancelled: null` both mean "not cancelled". In addition, `WorkflowReminder` has no index covering `(cancelled, scheduledDate)` or `scheduledDate`, and the cron now runs `findMany({ where: { cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { lte: ... } } })` every 15 minutes over a table that grows with every booking/workflow step, forcing a sequential scan each run. Consider `Boolean @default(false)` plus an index on the fields the cron filters on.

findings.title: Import block is not prettier-formatted and an unrelated commented-out block was re-indented
findings.body: `Prisma` is added to the import list without a trailing comma (line 9), and the previously type-only `import type { Prisma, PrismaPromise }` is turned into a value import even though both are only used in type positions. The same diff also re-indents the large commented-out `testAction` block (lines ~900-1010), which is unrelated to this change. The file is otherwise prettier-formatted, so the formatting check in CI will fail, and the comment reflow makes the diff hard to review.

findings.title: No test covers the new cancellation flow
findings.body: The new two-phase cancellation (mark `cancelled = true` on booking cancel/reschedule, then have the cron cancel at SendGrid and delete the row) is untested. The previous attempt at this fix (#6991) used the SendGrid API incorrectly and regressed silently in production; a test asserting that (a) cancelling a booking sets `cancelled = true` on its email reminders instead of deleting them and (b) the cron picks up only EMAIL reminders due within the window, cancels each and deletes the row even when one of them fails, would catch the loop-abort and filter problems noted above and prevent a repeat regression.
